raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old woman with no relevant medical history was referred to our institution for a progressive cognitive decline associated with episodic confusion of 6-week duration. She had difficulty naming objects and people and was unable to concentrate. She also manifested a progressive left-sided weakness with a tingling sensation that was particularly prominent in her lower limb. Her condition deteriorated on the day prior to presentation; and the patient's family knew of no comorbidities, particularly none that could be responsible for her immunosuppression. She was awake alert and partially oriented to her surroundings. Neurological examination revealed clear signs of cognitive impairment; her mini-mental state examination (MMSE) score was 21, indicating mild cognitive impairment, and confirmed left-sided weakness (strength of 4/5). There were no visual-spatial or cranial nerve functional deficits. An unusual leukopenia caused by lymphopenia was observed (white blood cells, 3.86 x 103/microL; lymphocytes, 0.73 x 103/microL [19%]; neutrophils, 2.54 x 103/microL [65.7%]; monocytes, 0.37 x 103/microL [9.6%]; eosinophils, 0.14 x 103/microL [3.6%]; and basophils, 0.02 x 103/microL [0.3%]). A stroke was suspected, and the patient was referred to the radiology department for an emergency computed tomography (CT) exam. CT demonstrated a subcortical focal area of low attenuation in the precentral gyrus (Figure 1). The patient was admitted to the neurology department with the misdiagnosis of subacute ischemic stroke.
A brain MRI revealed an area of hyperintensity on the T2-weighted FLAIR sequences and a hypointense area on the T1-weighted sequence in the precentral gyrus. This area had a particular gyriform pattern and affected only the WM; the cortical gray matter (GM) was spared. No enhancement was observed after administration of contrast media. The DWI sequence demonstrated no significant restriction of diffusion but a rim of hypointensity on the cortical side of lesions (Figure 2). This was confirmed to involve the subcortical U-fibers and is better appreciated in the SWI sequence (Figure 3).
The MRI results led us to discount the ischemic stroke diagnosis. These results indicated the presence of a pathological demyelinating condition. The subcortical U-fiber involvement with a well-demarcated peripheral border, the localization exclusively at the right precentral gyrus, and the presence of lymphopenia suggested that the patient might be suffering from PML caused by immunodeficiency. HIV tests showed a high viral load (6.75 x 105 HIV copies/mL) and a CD4+ count of less than 200 cells/mL, confirming a diagnosis of advanced AIDS. CSF analysis revealed a cell count of 17 cells/microL, protein level of 79 mg/dL, and glucose concentration of 56 mg/dL. CSF PCR demonstrated 5.73 x 104 JCV copies/mL. Appropriate therapy including HAART was initiated, and the brain MRI was repeated 2 months later. At that time, the patient's neurological condition was in steady decline, and her MMSE was 17/30. The patient continued to experience progressive difficulty in speaking, with signs of aphasia and progressive lower limb weakness that had begun to also affect her right lower limb. On MRI, we observed massive progression of T2-weighted FLAIR areas of hyperintensity extending to the precentral gyrus, semioval center, and corona radiata and partially to the parietal lobes (Figure 4).
The written informed consent was obtained for publication of this report and accompanying images.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old woman was referred with a 6-week history of progressive cognitive decline, episodic confusion, word-finding difficulty, and left-sided weakness and paresthesias.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 6 weeks preceding presentation, the patient experienced progressively worsening difficulty naming objects and people, impaired concentration, episodic confusion, and left-sided weakness accompanied by tingling most prominent in the left lower extremity, with acute worsening the day prior to admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: No known prior medical history or previously recognized causes of immunosuppression.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cognitive decline, anomia, confusion, left hemiparesis, and left lower limb paresthesia.

objective.physical_examination: Awake, alert, and partially oriented; Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score was 21/30, consistent with mild cognitive impairment. Motor examination confirmed left-sided hemiparesis (MRC strength 4/5) with intact cranial nerves and visuospatial function.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed leukopenia (WBC 3.86 x 10^3/µL) driven by lymphopenia (lymphocytes 0.73 x 10^3/µL [19%]; neutrophils 2.54 x 10^3/µL [65.7%]; monocytes 0.37 x 10^3/µL [9.6%]; eosinophils 0.14 x 10^3/µL [3.6%]; basophils 0.02 x 10^3/µL [0.3%]).
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was <200 cells/µL. Non-contrast head CT showed a focal subcortical hypodensity in the right precentral gyrus initially misdiagnosed as subacute ischemic stroke. Brain MRI revealed a non-enhancing gyriform T2/FLAIR-hyperintense, T1-hypointense lesion confined to the subcortical white matter and subcortical U-fibers of the right precentral gyrus sparing the cortical gray matter, without diffusion restriction on DWI and with a hypointense cortical-side rim on DWI/SWI. Lumbar puncture CSF analysis showed 17 cells/µL, protein 79 mg/dL, glucose 56 mg/dL, and positive CSF JC virus (JCV) quantitative PCR at 5.73 x 10^4 copies/mL.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) unmasking previously undiagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS, confirmed by positive CSF JC virus PCR (5.73 x 10^4 copies/mL), characteristic subcortical U-fiber demyelination on brain MRI (ruling out ischemic stroke), plasma HIV viral load of 6.75 x 10^5 copies/mL, and CD4+ T-cell count <200 cells/µL. Highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) was initiated; however, at 2-month follow-up, the patient exhibited progressive neurological deterioration (MMSE 17/30, worsening aphasia, and bilateral lower extremity weakness) with extensive radiological progression of T2/FLAIR white matter hyperintensities across the precentral gyrus, centrum semiovale, corona radiata, and parietal lobes.
